ref: Converse of cyclic quadrilateral theorem SolvedEx.1
stem:
In figure 3.51, chord LM \(\cong\) chord LN, \(\angle L = 35^\circ\) find

(i) \(m(\text{arc MN})\)

(ii) \(m(\text{arc LN})\)
solution:
(i) \(\angle L = \dfrac{1}{2} m(\text{arc MN})\) ......inscribed angle theorem.

\(\therefore 35 = \dfrac{1}{2} m(\text{arc MN})\)

\(\therefore 2 \times 35 = m(\text{arc MN}) = 70^\circ\)

(ii) \(m(\text{arc MLN}) = 360^\circ - m(\text{arc MN})\) ...... definition of measure of arc

\(= 360^\circ - 70^\circ = 290^\circ\)

Now, chord LM \(\cong\) chord LN

\(\therefore\) arc LM \(\cong\) arc LN

but \(m(\text{arc LM}) + m(\text{arc LN}) = m(\text{arc MLN}) = 290^\circ\) ..... arc addition property

\(m(\text{arc LM}) = m(\text{arc LN}) = \dfrac{290^\circ}{2} = 145^\circ\)

or, (ii) chord LM \(\cong\) chord LN

\(\therefore \angle M = \angle N\) ...... isosceles trinangle theorem.

\(\therefore 2\angle M = 180^\circ - 35^\circ = 145^\circ\)

\(\therefore \angle M = \dfrac{145^\circ}{2}\)

Now, \(m(\text{arc LN}) = 2 \times \angle M\)

\(= 2 \times \dfrac{145^\circ}{2} = 145^\circ\)
note: The book prints "isosceles trinangle theorem" — a misprint for 'triangle'. Transcribed as printed. The solution runs from printed p.70 onto p.71.

ref: Converse of cyclic quadrilateral theorem SolvedEx.2
stem:
In figure 3.52, chords PQ and RS intersect at T.

(i) Find \(m(\text{arc SQ})\) if \(m\angle STQ = 58^\circ\), \(m\angle PSR = 24^\circ\).

(ii) Verify, \(\angle STQ = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[m(\text{arc PR}) + m(\text{arc SQ})\right]\)

(iii) Prove that : \(\angle STQ = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[m(\text{arc PR}) + m(\text{arc SQ})\right]\) for any measure of \(\angle STQ\).

(iv) Write in words the property in (iii).
solution:
(i) \(\angle SPQ = \angle SPT = 58^\circ - 24^\circ = 34^\circ\) ....... exterior angle theorem.

\(m(\text{arc QS}) = 2\angle SPQ = 2 \times 34^\circ = 68^\circ\)

(ii) \(m(\text{arc PR}) = 2\angle PSR = 2 \times 24^\circ = 48^\circ\)

Now, \(\dfrac{1}{2}\left[m(\text{arc PR}) + m(\text{arc SQ})\right] = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[48 + 68\right]\)

\(= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 116 = 58^\circ\)

\(= \angle STQ\)

(iii) The book prints this step as a fill-in-the-blanks proof; the blanks are completed here.

\(\angle STQ = \angle SPQ + \angle PSR\) ....... exterior angle theorem of a triangle

\(= \dfrac{1}{2} m(\text{arc SQ}) + \dfrac{1}{2} m(\text{arc PR})\) ....... inscribed angle theorem

\(= \dfrac{1}{2}\left[m(\text{arc SQ}) + m(\text{arc PR})\right]\)

(iv) If two chords of a circle intersect each other in the interior of a circle then the measure of the angle between them is half the sum of measures of arcs intercepted by the angle and its opposite angle.
note: Part (iii) is printed with four empty boxes for the student to fill; the completed steps are supplied so the stored model answer is a whole proof rather than a hole. Parts (i), (ii) and (iv) are transcribed exactly as printed.

ref: Converse of cyclic quadrilateral theorem SolvedEx.3
stem: Prove that, if two lines containing chords of a circle intersect each other outside the circle, then the measure of angle between them is half the difference in measures of the arcs intercepted by the angle.
solution:
Given : Chords AB and CD intersect at E in the exterior of the circle.

To prove : \(\angle AEC = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[m(\text{arc AC}) - m(\text{arc BD})\right]\)

Construction : Draw seg AD.

Proof : The book leaves this proof to the student, directing: "Consider angles of \(\triangle AED\) and its exterior angle and write the proof." It is completed here.

\(\angle ADC\) is an exterior angle of \(\triangle AED\) at D.

\(\therefore \angle ADC = \angle AED + \angle DAE\) ....... exterior angle theorem of a triangle

\(\therefore \angle AEC = \angle ADC - \angle DAB\) ....... (\(\angle AED\) is \(\angle AEC\) and \(\angle DAE\) is \(\angle DAB\))

Now \(\angle ADC\) is inscribed in the circle and intercepts arc AC,

\(\therefore \angle ADC = \dfrac{1}{2} m(\text{arc AC})\) ....... inscribed angle theorem

and \(\angle DAB\) intercepts arc BD,

\(\therefore \angle DAB = \dfrac{1}{2} m(\text{arc BD})\) ....... inscribed angle theorem

\(\therefore \angle AEC = \dfrac{1}{2} m(\text{arc AC}) - \dfrac{1}{2} m(\text{arc BD})\)

\(\therefore \angle AEC = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[m(\text{arc AC}) - m(\text{arc BD})\right]\)
note: The book prints only the statement, Given, To prove and Construction, and asks the student to write the proof. The proof is supplied here so the stored model answer is complete; the Given / To prove / Construction lines are the book's own.
